Want to sell in Poland? We are icomSEO, a Polish agency based in Lublin with an office in Warsaw. The Polish market

## Poland is a large market. You win its customers in Polish.

Poland has around 37 million inhabitants. Polish shoppers search Google in Polish, compare prices and reviews, and buy from companies they trust. Translating your UK website is therefore not enough. You need Polish keywords, copy written for a Polish audience and campaigns set up specifically for the Polish market.

*   **Keywords for Poland**Keywords do not translate word for word. We research them in Senuto and Semrush, specifically for the Polish market.
*   **Copy by Polish writers**Our team writes product descriptions, category pages and articles in Polish, with SEO and Polish buying habits in mind.
*   **Trust at first glance**A Polish version of your website, local contact details, reviews and the payment methods Polish customers prefer, such as BLIK.

We know both markets

## How the Polish market differs from the UK market

We have run projects for the UK market, and Poland is our home market. These are the differences worth preparing for before you enter Poland.

| Area | United Kingdom | Poland |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Search engines | Google; Bing, with a smaller share | Google |
| Marketplaces and price comparison sites | Amazon.co.uk, eBay, Etsy, PriceRunner | Allegro, Ceneo |
| Payment methods | Debit and credit cards, PayPal, Apple Pay, Klarna | BLIK, Przelewy24, cards, bank transfer |
| Trust signals | Trustpilot, Feefo, Google reviews | Ceneo reviews, Google reviews |
| Currency and domain | GBP, .co.uk | PLN, .pl |
| EU and customs | Outside the EU, with its own customs and VAT rules | EU member state, part of the EU single market and customs union |
| Language and keywords | English | Polish, with dedicated Polish keywords |

### What we recommend preparing before you enter Poland

1.  A Polish version of your website, with localised content and prices in zloty (PLN).
2.  Polish payment methods, above all BLIK and Przelewy24.
3.  Delivery to InPost parcel lockers and a clear returns policy.
4.  Terms and conditions and customer service in Polish.
5.  A clear process for customs declarations, import VAT and any duties on goods shipped from the UK to Poland, as the UK is outside the EU.
6.  Conversion tracking in GA4 with GDPR-compliant consent management.

[Let's talk about preparing your launch in Poland →](https://icomseo.pl/uk/#contact)

Services

## What we do for you in Poland

Choose a single service or hand us all of your digital marketing in Poland.

### SEO in Poland

Technical SEO, Polish keywords, content and links. The aim is lasting visibility on Google in Poland.

### Google Ads in Poland

Search, Shopping, video and Performance Max campaigns for Polish customers. The ad account stays yours.

### Content in Polish

Website localisation, product descriptions, category pages, articles and ad copy by Polish writers.

### Websites and online shops

WordPress websites and WooCommerce, PrestaShop or Shopify shops, adapted for Polish customers.

### Meta Ads

Facebook and Instagram ads targeted at Poland, with conversion tracking.

### Analytics and tracking

GA4, Google Tag Manager and Consent Mode v2 in line with GDPR. You see what Poland brings you.

### Visibility in AI search

SEO, AEO and GEO, so that your brand also appears in Polish-language answers from AI search engines.

### E-commerce SEO

Categories, products and filters optimised for organic sales in the Polish market.

### Link building in Poland

Links from Polish websites that build your domain's authority on Google in Poland.

### SEO audit

An in-depth review of your website with a list of tasks ranked by impact.

### International SEO

Language versions, hreflang and local keywords for Poland and the other markets where you want to sell.

### Full-service marketing in Poland

Strategy, SEO, advertising, content and reporting in one place, with a single point of contact.

[Let's discuss the scope →](https://icomseo.pl/uk/#contact)

International experience

## SEO and digital marketing in 25 markets

We have run SEO and campaigns for clients in 25 markets across Europe, North America and Australia. Markets differ in their search engines, keywords and buying habits. That is why we prepare a separate strategy for each country.

*   **25**markets where we have experience
*   **10+**languages in which we run SEO and campaigns
*   **+228%**enquiries from foreign markets for our client Poland Premium

### SEO across several markets

*   Language versions of your website and correctly configured hreflang tags.
*   Keywords and content in the language of each market.
*   Technical SEO for international websites and online shops.
*   Besides Google, depending on the market, Bing or Seznam.

### Marketing across several markets

*   Google Ads and Meta Ads campaigns set up for each country.
*   Budgets and results tracked separately for each market.
*   Ad copy and landing pages in your customers' language.
*   We strengthen the channels that drive sales in each market.

results.markdown:
Poland Market Entry PR for International Brands | PR Insight

[← How we work](https://www.pr-insight.com/services)

05 — Market entry

# Poland Market Entry PR for International Brands

Launch in Poland with a story, message and media plan built for the market.

PR Insight plans and runs the communications side of entering Poland for UK, US and international brands: local positioning, Polish media relations, launch campaigns and Digital PR that build commercial credibility from day one.

Timeline

From 90 days

Format

Audit, sprint or retainer

Markets

US · UK ↔ Poland

Poland market context

## What entering Poland changes about the PR brief

Poland is highly connected and commercially mature. The opportunity is not to introduce people to a category they have never seen; it is to give Polish buyers, journalists and partners a credible reason to choose a new entrant. That usually means local evidence, Polish-language materials and a launch story tied to what the business is actually doing in-market.

95.9%

### of households have internet access

IAB Polska's 2024/2025 strategic report also records 67.4% of people buying online. Poland is a mature digital market, so an incoming brand competes for attention with established local and international names from day one.

[Source: IAB Polska, Internet 2024/2025](https://raportstrategiczny.iab.org.pl/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/Raport-Strategiczny-INTERNET-IAB-Polska-2024_2025.pdf)

75%

### of time online is spent on mobile

Gemius/PBI measured 29.7 million Polish internet users in Q4 2024, with mobile devices accounting for three quarters of total time online. Campaign pages, data assets and newsroom materials need to work on a phone first.

[Source: PBI, Polish internet in Q4 2024](https://pbi.org.pl/raporty/polski-internet-w-q4-2024/)

#15

### globally for adult English proficiency

Poland sits in EF's high-proficiency band, but this does not make an English press release locally relevant. Polish-language copy, local proof points and a spokesperson prepared for the Polish context still determine whether a pitch feels useful to an editor.

[Source: EF English Proficiency Index 2024, Poland](https://www.ef.com/assetscdn/WIBIwq6RdJvcD9bc8RMd/cefcom-epi-site/fact-sheets/2024/ef-epi-fact-sheet-poland-english.pdf)

International brands

## Poland market entry PR for international brands

Entering Poland requires more than translating an existing communications strategy. International brands need to establish local relevance, understand the Polish media landscape and give customers, journalists and business partners a clear reason to pay attention to a new entrant.

PR Insight helps UK, US and international companies entering or expanding in Poland turn their market-entry plans into credible local stories and targeted media campaigns.

Our approach combines

*   ### Market-specific positioning
    
    Adapting your messaging to the Polish market, category and competitive landscape.
    
*   ### Localised storytelling
    
    Developing narratives for Poland rather than simply translating a UK or US campaign.
    
*   ### Polish media relations
    
    Identifying and engaging the journalists and publications that influence your sector, customers and market.
    
*   ### Launch communications
    
    Building a PR programme around your actual Polish expansion, product launch, new office, investment, partnership or commercial milestone.
    
*   ### Executive and thought leadership positioning
    
    Using founders and senior experts to build credibility with Polish business, technology, trade and regional media.
    
*   ### Digital PR and SEO
    
    Creating campaigns that can generate relevant editorial coverage, links and stronger visibility in Polish search. For ongoing visibility after or alongside your launch, see [Digital PR in Poland](https://www.pr-insight.com/services/digital-pr-poland).
    

Whether you are entering Poland for the first time, opening a local office, launching a product or expanding an existing operation, we build the communications strategy around what is genuinely relevant to the Polish market.

The result: a launch that feels local, credible and newsworthy — while supporting your wider commercial market-entry objectives.

Market entry vs ongoing Digital PR

### Market-entry PR

A time-bound launch workstream: positioning, localisation, media mapping and the announcement itself, built around a real entry milestone such as an office opening, investment or product launch.

### Ongoing Digital PR in Poland

A continuous programme for brands already active in Poland: always-on media relations and campaigns that earn coverage, links and branded search over time. That is our [Digital PR in Poland](https://www.pr-insight.com/services/digital-pr-poland) service.

[Planning to enter the Polish market? Let's talk →](https://www.pr-insight.com/contact)

The communications workstream

## From market understanding to a credible Poland launch

Market-entry PR connects the commercial reason for entering Poland with a story that Polish media, buyers and partners can understand and trust.

1.  01
    
    ### Understand the Polish market
    
    We review the audience, competitors, category language and business milestones that should shape the communications brief.
    
2.  02
    
    ### Localise the story
    
    We replace home-market assumptions with Polish proof points, relevant messages and press materials written for local readers.
    
3.  03
    
    ### Identify the right media
    
    We prioritise the journalists and outlets that influence your buyers, sector, recruitment market or regional footprint in Poland.
    
4.  04
    
    ### Build journalist relationships
    
    Targeted briefings, useful commentary and responsive follow-up establish trust beyond a single launch announcement.
    
5.  05
    
    ### Launch the campaign
    
    We sequence the announcement, founder profile, sector angles and Digital PR activity around your real entry milestones.
    
6.  06
    
    ### Measure coverage and impact
    
    Reporting covers relevant media, message pull-through, links, branded search signals and the next opportunities created by the launch.
    

PR Insight leads the communications and media-relations part of market entry. We do not provide legal, tax, regulatory or corporate-establishment advice.

*   —British brands entering Poland
*   —US and international brands expanding into Poland
*   —Founders and in-house teams needing local expertise
